content.text:
The screen you saw, with Home squeezed into the left half and the printer chat on the right, only ever appeared in the test harness. The real app doesn't do it. I fixed the harness so it opens the printer chat the same way the app does, and added a check that fails if the chat ever leaves Home visible again.

**What was wrong.** In the real app, opening a printer chat goes through the shell, the code that manages the main window. The shell hides Home and the project tabs and gives the chat the whole window. Several harness test modes skipped the shell and showed the chat panel directly, so Home stayed on screen next to it. No person sees that layout. I opened the printer chat in the real app three different ways, and each time it covered the whole window, as the design canvas shows.

**What changed.** The changes are in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` and `tests/shell/server_sheet_scenario.inc` (27 lines added, 7 removed). A new helper, `open_printer_chat`, now opens the chat for every test that used to open the panel directly:
- It closes any chat that's already open and waits until the close has fully finished, because the shell won't open a second chat while one is open.
- It opens the chat through the shell.
- It checks that the chat is showing and that Home is hidden.

Product code is untouched.

**Test results.**
- **Printer setup mode:** 348 checks pass, 0 fail. When I put the old direct opening back, 6 of the new "chat covers Home" checks failed, so the check does catch the bug.
- **Print host check mode:** passes.
- **Printer chat sheet mode:** passes. In 2 of my first 4 runs of this mode the harness crashed on exit after every check had passed. I couldn't make it happen again: 0 crashes in 6 runs under the debugger, and 0 in 16 runs comparing the old harness with the new one, 8 each. It wrote no crash report, so I can't say whether my change has anything to do with it.
- **Connect skill mode:** 3 checks fail (`skill_add_settled`, `connect_skill_printer_added`, `connect_skill_comes_with_printer_add`). The unchanged harness on jusprin-dev fails the same 3, so they were broken before this change. The new checks pass in this mode.
- **Network check mode:** not run, because it needs Bambu's real plug-in.

**Still open.** I haven't looked into the 3 connect skill failures. The worktree is at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/harness-printer-chat-shell`, and its harness binary is now built from the fixed source.

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". git add tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp tests/shell/server_sheet_scenario.inc && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Shell harness: open the printer chat through the shell, as the app does

Several shell harness modes (--printer-setup, --printer-chat-sheet,
--print-host-check, --printer-network-check, --printer-connect-skill)
called PrinterPanel::open directly. That shows the panel but skips the
shell, which in the app hides Home and the project tabs and gives the
chat the whole window. So the harness window showed Home squeezed into
the left half with the chat beside it, a layout no person ever sees.
The real app was checked by opening the printer chat three ways; each
time the chat covered the whole window.

A new helper, open_printer_chat, opens the chat through
ShellController::open_printer_conversation, the path Home and the header
use. The shell opens no chat while one is open, so the helper first
closes an open chat and waits until its close (which finishes on a later
event turn) is done. It then checks that the chat is shown and that Home
is hidden.

Tested on macOS:
- --printer-setup: 348 checks pass, 0 fail. With the old direct opening
  put back, 6 of the new "chat covers Home" checks fail.
- --print-host-check and --printer-chat-sheet: pass.
- --printer-connect-skill: the new checks pass; 3 other checks
  (skill_add_settled, connect_skill_printer_added,
  connect_skill_comes_with_printer_add) fail, the same 3 that fail on
  the unchanged harness.
- --printer-network-check: not run, it needs Bambu's real plug-in.
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin && git merge --ff-only claude/harness-printer-chat-shell && git log --oneline -2 && git status --short | grep -v '^??'
